subject: Vendor swap: seat-credit exchange proposal + runtime compatibility clarifications
messages:
From: Claire Reynolds <c.reynolds@glacialtech.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@glacialtech.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T09:12:00Z
Subject: Pricing alignment request + runtime questions

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — we appreciated the demo and the runtime perf numbers. As we discussed, GlacialTech is evaluating a potential vendor swap at the end of our current contract (Q4). A few things we need to validate before we can move forward with an internal recommendation: 

1) A clear seat-credit structure or upfront credit to offset migration costs (we model a 6–9 month TCO impact).
2) Confirmation on runtime compatibility for our existing model variants (mainly conv-sparse models, 8-bit quantized).
3) A simple migration SLA for pilot/prod (timeouts, rollback window, and a short escalation path).

Can you share a short proposal that maps credits to usage tiers and a compatibility checklist? If you can include any headlines on concessions (one-time migration credit vs. monthly rebate), that would help our procurement team.

Also looping Daniel to ensure ops-level questions are captured.

Best,
Claire
Claire Reynolds
Director of ML Platform
GlacialTech

Subject: Re: Pricing alignment request + runtime questions

Claire — thank you, and great to meet you both today. Attached is a compact proposal that addresses the three items you called out: seat-credit exchange tiers, an initial compatibility matrix, and a pilot SLA snapshot. High level: 

- Seat-credit exchange: one-time onboarding credit equal to 25% of estimated first-quarter hosted spend for customers who commit to a 12-month reserved capacity agreement. For smaller pilots we can convert that into a per-seat credit applied over the first 90 days.
- Migration concession options: (A) Upfront credit (the 25% above) or (B) tiered monthly rebate for the first 3 months scaled to usage velocity. We recommend option A for lower friction.
- Runtime compatibility: preliminary check — conv-sparse models with 8-bit quantization run on our dedicated runtime with minor kernel fallbacks; latency uplift <12% on our T4/RTX pools in our verification tests. We'll need a small artifact (one representative model + 512 token profile) to validate exactly.

Next steps I suggest:
1) You share a representative model artifact and sample traffic profile (peak qps + seq length).
2) We run a 5–7 day perf validation and provide final latency/cost delta.
3) If results align, we issue a term-sheet with the chosen concession option and an onboarding milestone plan.

I've attached two files: the seat-credit proposal PDF (compact) and the runtime-compatibility matrix CSV. Marcus is cc'd to help tighten the commercial language if you want a direct concession number to run by procurement.

Would you be available for a short sync (30m) tomorrow to agree the artifact and pilot window?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan

Priya — quick internal note to capture constraints before we offer anything firm to GlacialTech: 

- The 25% onboarding credit should be capped at the first-quarter estimated spend or $250k, whichever is lower. Protects margin on large deals.
- For pilots < $50k ARR equivalent, prefer converting credits into usage discounts over 90 days to avoid complex reconciliation.
- Legal: any credit that requires clawback needs a 6–9 month audit window; loop in Legal if procurement pushes for shorter.

Connor, can you confirm we have the T4/RTX perf runs readily available in the perf-suite so we can promise the 5–7 day validation window? I want to avoid a slipped timeline once Claire sends the artifact.

Thanks,
